data.title: Which of the following muscles is innervated by the suprascapular nerve?
data.teaching: The suprascapular nerve (C5–C6, upper trunk of the brachial plexus) innervates the supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles.
data.reference: CIPS Examination Information Bulletin (2019 Edition), WIP Board of Examination — sample question 7, p. 16.
data.learningObjective: Recall the motor innervation of the suprascapular nerve.

sourceAudit.claim: The suprascapular nerve innervates the infraspinatus (and supraspinatus).
sourceAudit.verification: Official sample question with published answer A.

reviewNotes: Official bulletin sample question, included as scaffold seed content.

options.explanation: Correct. The suprascapular nerve supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus (Bulletin sample Q7, p. 16).
Innervated by the upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5–C7), not the suprascapular nerve (Bulletin sample Q7, p. 16).
Innervated by the axillary nerve (Bulletin sample Q7, p. 16).
Innervated by the axillary nerve (Bulletin sample Q7, p. 16).

data.title: Which artery lies close to the ilioinguinal nerve?
data.teaching: A branch of the deep circumflex iliac artery travels in close relation to the ilioinguinal nerve and is a useful sonographic landmark.
data.reference: CIPS Examination Information Bulletin (2019 Edition), WIP Board of Examination — sample question 8, p. 16.
data.learningObjective: Identify the vascular landmark adjacent to the ilioinguinal nerve.

sourceAudit.claim: A branch of the deep circumflex iliac artery lies close to the ilioinguinal nerve.
sourceAudit.verification: Official sample question with published answer C.

reviewNotes: Official bulletin sample question, included as scaffold seed content.

options.text: Branch of the superior ilioinguinal artery
options.explanation: No such named vessel is the described landmark (Bulletin sample Q8, p. 16).
An upper-abdominal vessel, anatomically remote from the ilioinguinal nerve (Bulletin sample Q8, p. 16).

options.text: Branch of the deep circumflex iliac artery
options.explanation: Correct. The deep circumflex iliac artery branch accompanies the nerve between the abdominal wall muscle layers (Bulletin sample Q8, p. 16).
No such named vessel; the iliohypogastric is a nerve, not an artery (Bulletin sample Q8, p. 16).

data.title: Where can the pudendal nerve be readily found?
data.teaching: The pudendal nerve is most readily visualised medial to the ischial spine, between the sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments.
data.reference: CIPS Examination Information Bulletin (2019 Edition), WIP Board of Examination — sample question 13, p. 17.
data.learningObjective: Localise the pudendal nerve for ultrasound-guided block.

sourceAudit.claim: The pudendal nerve is readily found medial to the ischial spine.
sourceAudit.verification: Official sample question with published answer D.

reviewNotes: Official bulletin sample question, included as scaffold seed content.

options.text: In the sacral plexus under piriformis
options.explanation: The pudendal nerve is not reliably imaged at this level (Bulletin sample Q13, p. 17).
The nerve does not course within the inferior gemellus (Bulletin sample Q13, p. 17).
The standard sonographic window is medial to, not under, the ischial spine (Bulletin sample Q13, p. 17).
Correct. The nerve lies medial to the ischial spine, between the sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments, near the internal pudendal vessels (Bulletin sample Q13, p. 17).
